purpose: Add one non-overlapping matched real-HUGSIM turning window under the existing frozen SparseDrive input contract. This characterizes task-level domain variation; it is not an equivalence pass/fail test.

selection.selection_basis: Earliest eight-frame 2 Hz window after the prior window ending at frame 54 for which all five fully warmed source-derived commands are left and the real camera-rig pose changes heading by more than 30 degrees across the window.
selection.selection_independence: Uses only the already identified real-source camera-rig poses and future route; no HUGSIM render, SparseDrive output or domain-difference result from this window was inspected.

held_fixed: official sample archive and scene identity
source timestamps, six-camera intrinsics and declared camera poses
SparseDrive-S Stage2 checkpoint, config and local adapter
receiver reset, temporal warm-up and camera order
pose-derived ego state, source-derived command and recorded future-path reference
changed_relative_to_prior_matched_window: real route geometry changes from near-straight/turn-entry to sustained left turn

primary: fully warmed real-versus-HUGSIM native plan ADE and endpoint distance
signed final forward and lateral differences
reality_reference_diagnostic: real-input plan ADE/FDE to the recorded camera-rig future path
HUGSIM-input plan ADE/FDE to the same recorded camera-rig future path

interpretation_rules: Only fully warmed frames may characterize matched AD-response domain difference.
A domain difference above repeat noise establishes a measurable receiver response difference, not a credibility failure.
No real-sim equivalence acceptance threshold will be invented from this window.
Recorded human/ego motion is a reality-derived descriptive reference, not the unique correct plan.
If selected mode differs between real and simulation, raw forward difference is reported with mode identity and is not interpreted as a maneuver-independent risk value.
Pixel similarity is not used as a substitute for task-output similarity.
The prior straight/turn-entry and new turning windows remain two windows from one reconstruction, not evidence of cross-scene generality.
strongest_allowed_claim: A second, motion-distinct matched factual real-HUGSIM SparseDrive response distribution was measured under the same receiver contract.
claims_to_reject: The two windows establish a universal real-sim equivalence threshold.
A lower trajectory error to the recorded ego path proves that the corresponding input domain is more realistic.
The result proves SparseDrive correct, HUGSIM credible in general, or an AD system safe.
